name: thirdparty-atomic

source.attribution: Atomic Red Team™ by Red Canary, MIT License. Command strings extracted from atomics/<technique>/<technique>.yaml executor blocks with input-argument defaults substituted; this is a derived subset.

provenance: THIRD-PARTY corpus — 203 real ATT&CK attack/benign commands from Atomic Red Team @ 2c63affb3b (MIT), across 45 techniques. Nobody at askalf wrote these. Labels assigned by SECURITY PRINCIPLE per ATT&CK technique (block=execution/impact/exfil/persistence/cred/evasion/C2, approve=dual-use, allow=discovery), NOT by "it's in Atomic Red Team". Only techniques with a principled verdict are imported; 16 had no base YAML, 2 test commands were dropped for unresolved placeholders, and 10 commands in allow/approve techniques were dropped because they were actually RCE download-cradles (not benign — they belong in no benign set), and 2 samples carry a documented per-sample label correction (see the sample's `relabeled` field, and SAMPLE_OVERRIDES in the builder) where the technique-level verdict did not fit the specific command. The allow set (discovery) is a genuine precision test from the same source as the attacks. Each sample carries an `axis` tag: 'command-semantic' (redstamp's axis) vs 'opaque-binary' (running a pre-staged .exe/.dll — out of a command-string firewall's reach, a documented limit, not a miss).

relabeled.reason: Writes a text file to the Desktop. A ransom note is an artefact OF ransomware, but the command is an ordinary file write — blocking `echo text > file` would be indiscriminate. Detecting it would mean matching ransom-note filenames, i.e. chasing indicators rather than mechanisms.

Password-protects an archive of the user's own test file. Encrypting your own data is legitimate backup behaviour; only encryption aimed at SYSTEM/credential files is ransomware-shaped (and that form is blocked). Dual-use → escalate, not block.
